```text
# PR #4929: Patch: the Call to Chaos a Training Grounds Call adds to a hand each turn may be Glitch, as every other card generated into a hand may

Closes #4845

## What changed

Two places in the engine added a random card from a pool to a hand without making R673's Glitch roll. Both now make it.

- **TG #39, entry 9** (`crates/engine/src/subsystems/call_to_chaos_training_grounds.rs`, `add_random_call`). The Call to Chaos added at the start of each of the caster's turns now passes the game state as the Glitch odds (`Some(&*ctx.sink.state)`), where it used to pass `None`. This is the same call `add_random_from_catalog` and `shuffle_random` make.
- **S #150, entry 4** (`crates/engine/src/subsystems/call_to_chaos_stinky.rs`, `build_acclaimed`). This is the neighbour the issue asked to check, and it had the same defect: it picked through plain `pick_unique`. It now picks through `pick_generated_unique(…, Some(&*ctx.sink.state), …)`. The Refresh after it reads the card that actually reached the hand, so a Glitch refreshes its printed (0).
- **Spec.**
  - A new ruling `spec/rulings/R4845000.md` and its paragraph in `spec/pending/4845.md`.
  - A "Since issue #4845" sentence added to R3135000 and to R1882002.
  - §8.11 row 39 and §8.10 row 150 now say the card may be Glitch on R673's odds.

The extra draw only happens once `system_plays` is above 0, because `glitch_or_not` returns early otherwise. A game with no System play draws exactly as before. All three R382 Grape ids are Classic+ cards, so S #150's Stinkyscape-only pool never makes the extra Grape roll; the only new draw is R673's.

## Tests

Each new test fails without the fix: I reversed the engine diff and saw both fail, then put it back.
- `c039_…::tests::base::r4845000_r673_the_call_entry_alternate_adds_may_be_glitch`: with odds set to certain, the caster's next turn adds one Glitch and no Call, and the opponent's hand gets none. Without the fix, a Call is added.
- `c150_…::tests::base::r4845000_r673_the_acclaimed_unit_may_be_glitch_and_refreshes_its_printed_zero`: with certain odds, entry 4 adds Glitch and mana ends at 10 − 4 + 0. Without the fix, `left: "stinkyscape-026"  right: "classic-t-glitch"`.

Commands I ran and what they printed:
- `cargo fmt --check`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine -p jackioh-cards --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-cards c039_call_to_chaos_training_grounds_edition`: 27 passed. `c150_call_to_chaos_stinky_edition`: 25 passed. `t_glitch_glitch`: 10 passed.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' glitch`: 26 + 1 passed.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai training_grounds`: 17 passed.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: "2591 rulings, 6405 proofs, 78333 citations in 5027 files, 35380 links: ok".
- `cargo jackioh patches check`: ok.
- `cargo jackioh catalog check`: ok.
- `cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts`: exit 0, 23,963 passed, 0 failed, and `apps/web/src/wire` was left clean.
- I did not run the workspace-wide clippy or the web tests. Nothing under `apps/` changed.

## Patch fragment: none, because classify found no card playing differently

I ran the real classifier with stage 2.
- **Base binary:** built from the merge base `13e90a64c0` in a detached worktree, with its own target dir, because `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is shared here.
- **Head:** stage 2 requires the root checkout's `HEAD` to be the head, and I must not commit in this worktree. So I made a commit object of the working tree through a temporary index; it sits on no branch. I checked it out detached in a second worktree and passed that as `--root`. Its content was confirmed identical to this worktree's.
- **Result:** `classify --base origin/main --head HEAD --parent-bin … --claims --json` printed `kind: internal`, `cards: []`, `rule: false`, `stage2: ran`, `problems: []`.
- **So:** a `plays` claim on either card would turn `rust (classify)` red, and leaving one out is what passes. I wrote no fragment, as plan step 10 says. Both temporary worktrees and the base target dir are removed.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **S #150 is fixed here, not split into its own issue.** R673's "added from a pool" leaves it no exemption, and the issue asked for it to be checked in the same change. The alternative was a separate issue.
- **Replays keep no old reading.** I followed R3135000's precedent: a replay that played a System card and then hit one of these entries folds to a different hash and is refused as `rules_changed` (R767000). The alternative was branching the engine's start-of-turn step by catalog version, for a draw that only happens after a System play.
- **A Glitch Acclaimed Unit refreshes 0.** "Refresh mana so you can play it" reads the card added, so the Refresh reads Glitch's printed cost. The alternative was refreshing the cost of the Acclaimed Unit that was picked.
- **Entry 10's recast (`cast_random_call_to_chaos`) is unchanged.** It is a cast, and R673 exempts casts.

## Worth a second look

- **No player-facing patch note.** Because classify confirms no card plays differently, no patch note will list this fix. A person decides whether that is acceptable.
- **The new draw only matters after a System play.** It shifts the rng only once a System card has been played. No committed fixture holds `systemPlays`, and the full workspace suite (golden replays and the fuzz-based tests included) passed unchanged.

Built and checked on `claude-7`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 10 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.
```
